terms.definition: The 5GC control-plane function handling registration, connection and mobility management, and NAS signaling termination for the UE.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15 as part of the service-based 5GC architecture, splitting MME responsibilities.

terms.definition: The 5GC function that performs authentication of the UE, working with the UDM/ARPF to execute 5G-AKA or EAP-AKA procedures.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15 as a dedicated authentication function separated from the HSS role in EPC.

terms.definition: The fraction of transport blocks received in error, used as a target metric for link adaptation and MCS selection.
terms.evolution: Target BLER operating points were refined in NR (Rel-15) to support ultra-reliable low-latency (URLLC) services.

terms.definition: A contiguous subset of the cell bandwidth that a UE is configured to operate within at a given time, enabling power-saving and mixed numerologies.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15 as an NR-only concept with no direct LTE equivalent.

terms.definition: The combination of multiple component carriers to increase a UE's effective bandwidth and peak data rate.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-10 as the defining LTE-Advanced feature; extended to NR intra- and inter-band CA from Rel-15 onward.

terms.definition: UE feedback indicating the highest modulation and coding scheme the current channel conditions can support.
terms.evolution: NR (Rel-15) added wideband and subband CQI reporting tied to configurable CSI reporting settings.

terms.definition: A configurable downlink reference signal used for channel quality measurement, beam management, and mobility measurements.
terms.evolution: Introduced in LTE Rel-10 for CoMP; substantially extended in NR (Rel-15) for beam management with mmWave.

terms.definition: UE- or beam-specific reference signal transmitted alongside data channels to enable coherent channel estimation for demodulation.
terms.evolution: NR (Rel-15) added configurable DMRS density and front-loaded symbols to support low-latency demodulation.

terms.full_name: E-UTRA Absolute Radio Frequency Channel Number
terms.definition: The channel numbering scheme used to identify carrier frequencies for LTE bands.
terms.evolution: Defined in Rel-8; range was extended in later releases as new LTE bands were added.

terms.definition: A non-standalone 5G deployment option where a UE connects simultaneously to an LTE eNodeB (master) and an NR gNodeB (secondary), sharing an EPC core.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15 as the first commercially deployed 5G architecture ahead of standalone 5GC rollout.

terms.definition: The signaling protocol over the F1 interface between a gNodeB-CU and gNodeB-DU in a disaggregated RAN deployment.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15 to enable the CU/DU functional split standardized for NG-RAN.

terms.definition: A retransmission mechanism combining forward error correction with ARQ, using soft-combining of failed and retransmitted data.
terms.evolution: NR (Rel-15) reduced round-trip time versus LTE and added support for up to 16/32 HARQ processes for high-throughput scheduling.

terms.definition: The Layer 2 sublayer responsible for scheduling, HARQ, and multiplexing of logical channels onto transport channels.
terms.evolution: Re-specified for LTE (TS 36.321) and NR (TS 38.321), gaining features like multi-numerology scheduling in NR.

terms.definition: An index mapping to a specific modulation order and code rate combination applied to a transport block.
terms.evolution: NR (Rel-15) added 256-QAM tables and, in later releases, 1024-QAM for high-SNR scenarios.

terms.definition: The broadcast system information carrying the minimal set of parameters a UE needs before it can read further scheduling information.
terms.evolution: In NR (Rel-15) the MIB is carried on the PBCH within the SSB rather than on PDSCH as in LTE.

terms.definition: The EPC control-plane node handling NAS signaling, idle-mode UE tracking, bearer activation/deactivation, and authentication for LTE.
terms.evolution: A Rel-8 EPC function; its role is split into AMF (mobility) and SMF (session) in the 5G core.

terms.definition: The 5GC reference point between the NG-RAN and the AMF, carrying NGAP signaling.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15 as the 5G equivalent of the S1-MME interface.

terms.definition: The 5GC reference point carrying user-plane GTP-U traffic between the NG-RAN and the UPF.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15 as the 5G equivalent of the S1-U interface.

terms.definition: The 5GC function that securely exposes network capabilities and events to external third-party applications.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15; expanded in later releases to expose more granular QoS and analytics events.

terms.definition: The signaling protocol over the N2 interface between the gNodeB and the AMF, carrying UE context and PDU session management.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15 as the NG-RAN/5GC counterpart to S1AP.

terms.full_name: NR Absolute Radio Frequency Channel Number
terms.definition: The channel numbering scheme used to identify carrier frequencies in NR across FR1 and FR2.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15 with a wider global raster than EARFCN to accommodate FR1 and FR2 bands.

terms.definition: The 5GC function that provides service discovery, allowing network functions to register and discover each other over the service-based interface.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15 alongside the service-based architecture (SBA) that defines 5GC.

terms.definition: A 5G deployment architecture where NR radio is anchored by an existing LTE/EPC control plane, most commonly realized as EN-DC.
terms.evolution: Defined in Rel-15 as the fast-to-market 5G option, expected to be phased out as SA/5GC deployments mature.

terms.definition: The physical channel that carries the MIB, allowing a UE to acquire the minimum system information needed to access a cell.
terms.evolution: In NR (Rel-15), the PBCH is transmitted as part of the SSB and repeated across beams for beam sweeping.

terms.definition: The 5GC function that provides policy rules for QoS, charging, and traffic steering to the SMF and other network functions.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15 as the 5GC evolution of the EPC PCRF.

terms.definition: The physical channel carrying downlink control information (DCI) that schedules PDSCH/PUSCH resources and delivers other control commands.
terms.evolution: NR (Rel-15) replaced the fixed CFI-based control region with flexible CORESETs and search spaces.

terms.definition: The Layer 2 sublayer providing header compression, ciphering, integrity protection, and in-order delivery for user and control plane data.
terms.evolution: Extended in NR (Rel-15) with duplicate detection/discard to support dual connectivity and split bearers.

terms.definition: The main downlink data-bearing physical channel, carrying user-plane and higher-layer control data scheduled via PDCCH.
terms.evolution: NR (Rel-15) added flexible mapping types and mini-slot scheduling on PDSCH for low-latency use cases.

terms.definition: Layer 1 of the radio protocol stack, responsible for modulation, coding, and mapping of transport channels onto physical resources.
terms.evolution: WCDMA-based in UMTS, OFDMA/SC-FDMA in LTE (Rel-8), and a flexible OFDM numerology with mmWave support in NR (Rel-15).

terms.definition: UE feedback recommending the precoding matrix the network should apply for closed-loop MIMO transmission.
terms.evolution: NR (Rel-15) introduced Type I and Type II codebooks, with Type II giving finer-grained precoding feedback for massive MIMO.

terms.definition: The uplink physical channel used by the UE to initiate random access, enabling uplink timing synchronization and initial access.
terms.evolution: NR (Rel-15) introduced a 2-step RACH procedure alongside the traditional 4-step procedure, finalized in Rel-16.

terms.definition: The basic unit of frequency-domain resource allocation, consisting of 12 consecutive subcarriers over one slot.
terms.evolution: NR (Rel-15) kept the 12-subcarrier PRB definition but made its bandwidth numerology-dependent (15/30/60/120 kHz SCS).

terms.definition: The sidelink physical channel used to broadcast synchronization and system information directly between UEs in D2D/V2X communication.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-12 for ProSe D2D; extended in Rel-14 for V2X and again in Rel-16 for NR sidelink.

terms.definition: The physical channel carrying uplink control information such as HARQ feedback, scheduling requests, and CSI reports.
terms.evolution: NR (Rel-15) introduced multiple PUCCH formats spanning 1-14 OFDM symbols for flexible numerologies.

terms.definition: The main uplink data-bearing physical channel, used for user-plane data and, when needed, uplink control information.
terms.evolution: NR (Rel-15) introduced configured grant (grant-free) transmission on PUSCH for latency-critical traffic.

terms.definition: A logical connection between the UE and the network providing a defined QoS treatment for either signaling (SRB) or user data (DRB).
terms.evolution: NR (Rel-15) retained the SRB/DRB model while adding split bearers for dual connectivity.

terms.definition: UE feedback indicating the number of spatial layers (transmission rank) that can be supported for MIMO transmission.
terms.evolution: NR (Rel-15) extended RI reporting to support up to 8 layers for single-user MIMO.

terms.definition: The Layer 2 sublayer providing segmentation, ARQ retransmission, and in-sequence delivery between MAC and PDCP.
terms.evolution: Simplified in NR (Rel-15) by removing concatenation, relying more on MAC-layer multiplexing.

terms.definition: The Layer 3 protocol that manages connection establishment, mobility, and configuration of the radio interface between the UE and the network.
terms.evolution: Present since UMTS; re-specified for E-UTRA in Rel-8 (TS 36.331) and NR in Rel-15 (TS 38.331), adding RRC_INACTIVE in NR.

terms.definition: A UE measurement of the average power of reference signal resource elements, used for cell selection, reselection, and handover decisions.
terms.evolution: Extended in NR (Rel-15) with SS-RSRP and CSI-RSRP variants measured on the SSB and CSI-RS respectively.

terms.definition: A UE measurement combining RSRP and received signal strength (RSSI) to indicate signal quality relative to total channel power.
terms.evolution: Extended in NR (Rel-15) with SS-RSRQ and CSI-RSRQ variants.

terms.definition: The signaling protocol over the S1-MME interface between eNodeB and MME, carrying context setup, handover, and paging procedures.
terms.evolution: Defined in Rel-8; its 5G counterpart is NGAP over the N2 interface.

terms.definition: A 5G deployment architecture where the gNodeB connects directly to the 5G core (5GC) without relying on an LTE anchor.
terms.evolution: Defined in Rel-15 alongside NSA; became the primary deployment target as 5GC and gNodeB maturity increased from Rel-16 onward.

terms.definition: Broadcast messages carrying cell configuration, neighbor cell, and access-control information beyond what the MIB provides.
terms.evolution: NR (Rel-15) introduced on-demand SIB delivery for infrequently needed system information.

terms.definition: A measurement expressing the ratio of desired signal power to interference and noise power, used to estimate achievable throughput.
terms.evolution: Reported as SS-SINR in NR (Rel-15) using SSB or CSI-RS resources.

terms.definition: The 5GC function responsible for PDU session establishment, IP address allocation, and UPF selection and control.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15, taking over the session-management portion of the EPC P-GW control plane.

terms.definition: The NR block combining PSS, SSS, and PBCH, transmitted periodically to enable cell search, synchronization, and beam management.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15 as the NR replacement for the separately-transmitted PSS/SSS/PBCH structure used in LTE.

terms.definition: The number of information bits contained in a transport block, derived from the MCS, allocated resource blocks, and layer count.
terms.evolution: NR (Rel-15) introduced a new TBS determination formula supporting a much wider range of allocation sizes than LTE.

terms.definition: The 5GC function that stores subscriber subscription data and generates authentication credentials, exposed via the UDR.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15, unifying subscriber data handling previously split across the HSS.

terms.definition: The 5GC user-plane node that performs packet routing, forwarding, QoS enforcement, and traffic reporting, with control via PFCP from the SMF.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15 to realize control/user-plane separation (CUPS), a pattern retrofitted to EPC in parallel.

terms.definition: The signaling protocol over the X2 interface between neighboring eNodeBs, used for handover preparation and interference coordination.
terms.evolution: Defined in Rel-8; evolved into XnAP for inter-gNodeB signaling in NR (Rel-15).

terms.definition: The signaling protocol over the Xn interface between NG-RAN nodes, supporting dual connectivity and mobility.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15 as the 5G counterpart to X2AP.

terms.definition: The LTE radio base station, combining the functions of the UMTS Node B and RNC into a single flat-architecture element that terminates the radio interface and connects directly to the EPC.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-8 as the sole radio element of E-UTRAN, replacing the Node B/RNC split used in UMTS.

terms.definition: The 5G NR base station, capable of connecting to both 5GC (via NG) and, in non-standalone mode, acting as a secondary node alongside an eNodeB.
terms.evolution: Introduced in Rel-15; gained a disaggregated CU/DU split (F1AP) and NTN-capable variants in later releases.
